title: Bounded acyclic flat models represent the proper coefficient map termwise
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small etale sites and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ and $\lambda:T_Wr_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r_B^*T_V$ for the canonical tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $q_r:T_VRr_{*,A}\to Rr_{*,B}T_W$ as the adjoint transpose under $r_B^*\dashv Rr_{*,B}$ of $T_W(\varepsilon_A)\circ\lambda^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon_A:r_A^*Rr_{*,A}\to1$ is the counit [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Let $C$ be a cochain complex of $A_W$-module sheaves, zero outside a finite interval, and put $C_B=C\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ termwise. Assume each $C^n$ is flat over $A_W$, meaning tensoring with it is exact; assume each $r_{*,A}C^n$ is flat over $A_V$; and assume for every $n$ and every $a>0$ that
$$R^ar_{*,A}(C^n)=0,\qquad R^ar_{*,B}(C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W)=0.$$
Then the canonical acyclic-complex comparison maps identify $Rr_{*,A}C$ and $Rr_{*,B}C_B$ with the degreewise complexes $r_{*,A}C$ and $r_{*,B}C_B$, respectively. The complexes $C$ and $r_{*,A}C$ are K-flat (tensoring them with any acyclic complex gives an acyclic total tensor complex). Under these specified identifications and the flat-model identifications for $T$, the named map $q_r(C)$ is represented by the termwise sheaf projection morphism
$$\pi_C:(r_{*,A}C)\otimes_{A_V}B_V\longrightarrow r_{*,B}(C\otimes_{A_W}B_W),$$
whose degree-$n$ morphism is adjoint to
$$r_B^*((r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\cong(r_A^*r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_W}B_W
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{A,C^n}\otimes1}C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W.$$
The identifications and this representation are natural in chain maps between complexes satisfying these hypotheses. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work in the existing constant-coefficient presentation Sheaf(T.smallEtaleTopology, ModuleCat A). Its abelian, Grothendieck, injective-resolution and flat-resolution instances are already provided by Mathlib and the adopted source library. Use the canonical upperStar/lowerStar adjunction and its derived adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No equivalence with the separate SheafOfModules presentation is required.

Boundedness gives IsStrictlyGE a and IsStrictlyLE b for C and its termwise direct image D. The braiding turns exactness of tensorRight into exactness of tensorLeft. The existing proved source theorem CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat therefore makes C and D K-flat. This theorem builds a bounded flat complex from its single-term flat complexes by finitely many distinguished triangles.

Identify the positive derived homology of each single sheaf with the ordinary right-derived functors by homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso. The hypotheses are thus rightAcyclic for each term of C and C_B. Apply the source-library isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic, the canonical bounded-below acyclic-complex computation [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. The proved compatibility ι_map_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_comp transports this to the unbounded right-derived unit. The homotopy quotient factors are isomorphisms, giving exactly the specified properAcyclicComparison maps.

For ordinary scalar extension E and exact faithful restriction U, construct E composed with U as tensorRight of the sheafified constant B-module, using the ordinary module balancing isomorphism and compatibility of sheafification with tensor. An acyclic K-flat complex stays acyclic after tensoring with any object; faithfulness and exactness of U reflect this acyclicity. Hence E preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms. Its canonical left-derived counit is invertible on K-flat complexes. Transport the derived E/U adjunction along the exact-restriction comparison and compare it with the actual chosen scalar adjunction exposed by EtaleDerivedScalarTensor. The derived unit factorization identifies the specified scalarExtensionRepresentative with the canonical counit composed with the unique comparison of left adjoints. Therefore both specified scalar representatives are isomorphisms. This needs no flatness of B.

The abstract derived-adjunction identity derivedε_fac_app identifies the adjunct of properAcyclicComparison with the ordinary complex counit followed by the geometric representative map. Use the normalization of scalarPullbackIso_existsUnique on the K-flat complex D, as recorded in [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection], and naturality of scalarExtensionRepresentative on the ordinary A-counit. Degreewise, mateEquiv_counit identifies the ordinary coefficient chain map with scalar/pullback reassociation followed by scalar extension of that A-counit. Naturality of the B-geometric representative and the same derived-counit identity for B then give equal B-adjuncts for the two sides of the displayed square. Injectivity of the B-adjunction hom equivalence proves the square with precisely the prescribed maps. The six factorization and naturality identities are combined by a proved generic adjunction pasting lemma before specialization, avoiding repeated concrete functor comparisons.

The coefficient mate is a natural transformation. The acyclic comparisons are composites of the natural homotopy quotient factors and the right-derived units. Scalar representatives are adjuncts of the natural ordinary scalar units and the exact-restriction quotient comparisons; naturality of the hom equivalence proves their naturality. The coefficient chain map is obtained by mapping the ordinary coefficient natural transformation to complexes. These naturality identities give all six equations for an arbitrary chain map, and hence for maps between the stipulated models.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GL6; bounded acyclic computation (015E), bounded flat K-flatness (06YQ), and derived adjunction normalization (0FND). The proof reuses the adopted source-library canonical unit/counit APIs directly and the existing scalarPullbackIso_existsUnique normalization.
proof_origin.note: All original public signatures remain unchanged. The acyclic and scalar representative definitions are assembled as generic natural transformations before direct specialization. The canonical unit, counit, and mate maps remain the same. A proved private categorical pasting lemma combines the six factorization, naturality, and normalization identities to check the concrete square once. Every new theorem is proved; no theorem or definition hole is introduced. The separate SheafOfModules cochain-model theorem is not used.
